doc.title: Barry Kernfeld interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 16, 2020

title: The online Grove edition and rewriting Nancy Wilson's entry
summary: Online publication removes space pressure, and entries like Nancy Wilson's are rewritten to cover her whole life, not just jazz.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Okay. Does the fact that the next thing’s going to be an on-line edition, you literally don’t have to worry about how heavy it’s going to be, how many pages you’re creating?

Yes. That’s a big factor. It takes off a lot of pressure because you don’t have to worry about publication cost. And you want to show some editorial sense as far as proportion and consistency and you don’t write 300 words about this person and 7000 about the next. You want to have a balance maintained, but you can add a lot of detail that I would have had to worry about twenty years ago and don’t have to worry about now. If it’s important I can put it in. I think the much bigger consideration now is it’s no longer a jazz dictionary. It’s now The New Grove Dictionary of Jazz a component of Grove Music

Online, a component of Oxford Music Online. Which means when we do Nancy Wilson, I just re-wrote her article that was maybe 350 or 400 words, now it’s probably a thousand, I didn’t count. Because we’re no longer writing about Nancy Wilson as a jazz musician. We’re about writing about Nancy Wilson as a jazz musician, as a popular musician, as an actress, as an entertainer on TV, as a host of the “Jazz Profiles” show, as a civil rights activist, as a member of the Minority Council on AIDS. We’re writing about her life now. And it’s way more interesting to do it that way, and it’s a way to not have to worry about putting someone in a jazz box, not have to worry about if this guy has an article in the general Grove Dictionary, should he also have an article in the jazz one and should it be different, because they’re all collected into one place now and it’s really, it’s a good thing.
